fields.description:
Latent robustness gap found by the LLM code review of Gerrit 1905 (C4).

## Context / Problem

`scripts/gen_config_reference.py::_lifecycle_index()` uses `dict.setdefault` when mapping a
canonical schema key to its lifecycle note, so if one canonical replacement key is ever the
target of MORE THAN ONE cfg deprecation alias and/or tombstone, only the first-encountered
note survives and the rest are silently dropped from the generated `docs/config-reference.md`.
Confirmed in code: both loops in `_lifecycle_index` call `index.setdefault(replacement, ...)`.

No collision exists today (each cfg replacement key is targeted exactly once across
`rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` + `tombstones()`), so current generated output is correct.
This is a defensive fix that stops a future deprecation from silently deleting doc content.

## Approach

Accumulate the notes per canonical key instead of `setdefault`: collect them into a list keyed
by replacement, then join them into the single `Lifecycle` table cell. The single-note case
must render byte-identically to today so `docs/config-reference.md` needs no regeneration and
the committed-tree drift oracle stays green.

## Scope

- `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` — rewrite `_lifecycle_index` to accumulate.
- `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` — add the held-out collision guards.

No other module reads `_lifecycle_index`; `docs/env-vars.md` is out of scope because its
generator only scans `src/rebar`.

## Testing

Held-out guards seed collisions by monkeypatching the generator's `_cfg_deprecations` /
`_cfg_tombstones` accessors onto a real schema key, then assert both notes survive into that
key's rendered table row:

- Two deprecated aliases sharing one replacement — both alias names appear in the row.
- One deprecated alias plus one tombstone sharing one replacement — both notes appear.
- Each guard is confirmed RED against unmodified `main` (the second note is absent) before
  the fix lands.
- Regression: the whole existing oracle, including the read-only committed-tree `--check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_lifecycle_index` accumulates every lifecycle note for a canonical key with no silent
  drop; checked by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py -q` passing the
  new collision guards.
- [x] A test seeds a 2-alias collision and asserts both notes appear in that key's
  `config-reference.md` row; checked by the same pytest run, and by observing it FAIL on
  unmodified `main` first.
- [x] `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py --check` exits 0 against the committed tree and
  the pre-existing oracle stays green; checked by that command plus the full
  `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` run.
- [x] Gates stay green; checked by `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting new=0 increased=0 stale=0.
